skill.name: lark-workflow-standup-report
skill.description: Generate a daily standup report from Lark calendar events and incomplete tasks using lark-cli.
skill.summary: Summarizes Lark meetings, pending tasks, conflicts, and free time for daily planning.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: The real concerns are fixed lark-cli command execution and parent-directory references to sibling skill files. Most static command findings are Markdown formatting false positives, and no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory references leave the skill package boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Package the shared Lark guidance as declared dependencies, or copy the required instructions into this skill. Avoid ../ reads from skill instructions.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes lark-cli commands against user calendar and task data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running lark-cli, and show the exact read scopes before authentication or data access.

remediation.issue: Reports may include sensitive calendar and task details.
remediation.suggestion: Default to narrow date ranges, avoid persisting raw command output, and summarize only the data needed for the report.

content.value_statement: Daily planning is slower when meetings and tasks live in separate Lark tools. This skill combines both into a clear standup report.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to authenticate with lark-cli for calendar and task access.
Fetches a Lark calendar agenda for today or a specified ISO date range.
Retrieves incomplete Lark tasks with due-date filtering and paging guidance.
Combines meetings and tasks into a standup-ready daily summary.
Maps time zones, RSVP states, conflicts, and free time into readable output.
limitations: Requires lark-cli and a signed-in Lark user account.
Uses read-only calendar and task scopes; it does not create or update records.
Natural-language dates must be converted to ISO 8601 values before commands run.
Large task lists may need paging or additional filtering.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team Standups
use_cases.description: Create a concise view of meetings, pending tasks, conflicts, and open time before a daily standup.

use_cases.title: Plan a Focused Workday
use_cases.description: Review accepted meetings and due tasks so priorities are clear before work starts.

use_cases.title: Review Schedule Load
use_cases.description: Check calendar density and task pressure for a specific day or week.

prompt_templates.title: Today Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to summarize my Lark calendar and incomplete tasks for today. Show meetings, due tasks, conflicts, and free time.

prompt_templates.title: Tomorrow Planning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standup report for tomorrow. Convert the date to ISO 8601 before running lark-cli commands.

prompt_templates.title: Specific Date Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my Lark schedule and incomplete tasks for 2026-03-26. Include RSVP status, overdue tasks, conflicts, and free slots.

prompt_templates.title: Weekly Workload Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current work week in Lark. Use calendar agenda and incomplete tasks. Group results by day and flag conflicts.

output_examples.input: Summarize today's standup report from Lark.
output: Conflict: product review overlaps with design sync.

output_examples.input: Create a report for tomorrow's schedule and pending work.
output: Tomorrow: 2 accepted meetings, 1 tentative meeting, and 4 tasks due soon.

output_examples.input: Review my current work week in Lark.
output: Monday and Wednesday have the highest meeting load.
Three tasks are due before Friday.
Tuesday afternoon has the best focus block.

best_practices: Confirm the target date before running lark-cli commands.
Limit task results by due date when the report does not need historical items.
anti_patterns: Do not pass natural-language dates directly to lark-cli.
Do not omit the incomplete-task filter for standup reports.
Do not include declined events in busy-time or conflict calculations.

faq.question: Does this skill require Lark access?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires lark-cli and a signed-in user with calendar and task read scopes.

faq.question: Can it change my calendar or tasks?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads agenda and task data only.

faq.question: What date formats should I use?
faq.answer: Use ISO 8601 dates or timestamps. Convert natural language dates before command execution.

faq.question: Does it include completed tasks?
faq.answer: It should use --complete=false for standup reports, so completed tasks are excluded.

faq.question: Can it summarize a full week?
faq.answer: Yes. Run agenda and task queries for the target range, then group results by day.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is packaged for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
